runtimeEvidence.detail: The first successful controlled service run sealed Gear, then Community and Manifest before any decision. The final controlled timer run reused exactly 2 Gear releases, 2 Community releases and 2 Manifests, classified 568 changed items, 568 changed sources and 7494 changed variants as high_risk_gear, passed shadow, returned manual_required and left the active generation-9 pointer unchanged.

Candidate deploy logged that the timer was enabled but not started; refresh event count remained 2 and timer/service stayed inactive. An explicit timer start at 19:20:55 CST triggered one service run, completed successfully at 19:23:09 CST, and scheduled the next systemd-owned run for 2026-07-12 18:43:06 CST.

Health truthfully reports blocked/manual_required with exact candidate identities, high_risk_gear, 40 winners, 319 rejected, zero empty, bounded Gear change counts, reused seal status, shadow pass for 40 specs, p95 836.599ms, max 1175.783ms and total shadow duration 35908.111ms; no raw SQL, DSN or traceback is exposed.

The first candidate attempt failed before Python because ProtectSystem=strict blocked /run/lock; the second failed bounded as REFRESH_ENVIRONMENT_FAILED because ProtectHome=true hid /home/ubuntu/.pgpass. Both attempts created zero refresh events or releases and left the pointer unchanged. ReadWritePaths=/run/lock and ProtectHome=read-only were added with tests; the exact sandbox then acquired both the file and PG leases and completed successfully.

At unchanged generation 9, 40/40 formal observed-only templates imported and resolved with zero failures; 11 Profiles resolved and 29 remained truthfully blocked, with combined p50 549.657ms, p95 646.944ms and max 696.928ms. Malformed, stale, missing-item and unknown-Catalyst cases stayed fail-closed while legacy Profile remained non-empty.

The controlled timer service exited 0 with Result=success, CPUUsageNSec 116643758000 and MemoryPeak 1502662656 bytes. wow-backend stayed active with NRestarts=0 and MemoryCurrent 122945536 bytes. Existing staging timers retained their schedules, no systemd units failed, and backend, refresh and Nginx warning/error counts since final deploy were all zero.
